units.literal: Second year spring first month—the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to erect a temple in Luoyang, assign left and right senior clerks, enlarge aides and attendants to ten men fully, annually nominate one aide each for censor and xiucai, add one hundred official riders and fourteen musicians, enfeoff son Rong as marquis of Pingle ting and Lun as marquis of Anle ting.

units.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
units.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.
units.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.

units.zh: 甲戌，以齊王冏爲大司馬、都督中外諸軍事，成都王穎爲大將軍、錄尚書事，河間王顒爲太尉。
units.en: Prince Jiong became grand marshal and commander-in-chief, Prince Ying general-in-chief with charge of the secretariat, and Prince Yong grand commandant on the jiaxu day.
units.literal: On the jiaxu day, Prince Jiong of Qi was made grand marshal and area commander for all military affairs within and without; Prince Ying of Chengdu was made general-in-chief and recorder of secretariat affairs; Prince Yong of Hejian was made grand commandant.

units.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
units.en: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.
units.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.

units.zh: 及穎將趙驤、石超戰于湨水，會等大敗，棄軍走。
units.en: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
units.literal: When Ying’s generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao battled at the Ju River, Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned the army and fled.

units.zh: 鎮東大將軍、齊王冏，征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，並以明德茂親，忠規允著，首建大策，匡救國難。
units.en: General-in-chief who guards the east Prince Jiong of Qi, general-in-chief who conquers the north Prince Ying of Chengdu, and general-in-chief who conquers the west Prince Yong of Hejian are men of shining virtue and eminent kinship whose loyal counsel stood the test; they first devised the great plan that delivered the state from disaster.
units.literal: General-in-chief who guards the east, Prince Jiong of Qi; general-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian—all with bright virtue as flourishing kin, loyal plans truly manifest, first established the great strategy and rectified and saved the state’s crisis.

units.zh: 秋八月壬午，立廣陵王遹爲皇太子，以中書監何劭爲太子太師，吏部尚書王戎爲太子太傅，衛將軍楊濟爲太子太保。
units.en: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Sima Yu, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
units.literal: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Prince Sima You of Guangling was established as crown prince; Director of the Secretariat He Shao was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Rong was made grand tutor of the heir apparent; General of the Guards Yang Ji was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

units.zh: 以廣陵王師劉寔爲太子太保，司空、隴西王泰錄尚書事。
units.en: Liu Shi became grand guardian to the crown prince, and Prince Tai of Longxi, still minister of works, took charge of secretariat business.
units.literal: Preceptor to the Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.

units.zh: 丙午，皇太子冠，丁未，見于太廟。
units.en: The crown prince came of age with the capping ceremony one day and was presented at the ancestral temple the next.
units.literal: On the bingwu day the crown prince underwent capping; on the dingwei day he appeared in the Grand Temple.

units.zh: 永平元年春正月乙酉朔，臨朝，不設樂。
units.en: On the yiyou new moon of the first month of spring in Yongping 1, the emperor held court without music.
units.literal: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Yongping, on the yiyou new moon, he attended court and did not set out music.

units.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」
units.en: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."
units.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”

units.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。
units.en: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.
units.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.

units.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。
units.en: She schemed with them against Minhuai.
units.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.

units.zh: 十二月，太子長子虨病，太子為虨求王爵，不許。
units.en: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Bin but was not granted it.

units.zh: 虨疾篤，太子為之禱祀求福。
units.en: As Bin grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
units.literal: When Bin's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

units.zh: 於是使尚書和郁等持節詣東宮，廢太子為庶人，太子改服出，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車，車武公澹以兵仗送太子及妃王氏、三子虨、臧、尚同幽於金墉城。
units.en: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
units.literal: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

units.zh: 殺太子母謝淑媛及虨母保林蔣俊。
units.en: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were executed.
units.literal: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were killed.

units.zh: 楊駿藉武帝之寵私，叨竊非據，賈謐乘惠皇之蒙昧，成此厲階，遂使悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷。
units.en: Yang Jun parlayed Emperor Wu’s favor into a post he never deserved; Jia Mi exploited Emperor Hui’s weakness and laid the steps to ruin—so Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.
units.literal: Yang Jun relied on Emperor Wu’s private favor and grasped what he should not have held; Jia Mi rode Emperor Hui’s dullness and made this stair of evil, so that Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.

units.zh: 十一月，大舉伐吳，遣鎮軍將軍、琅邪王伷出涂中，[24]安東將軍王渾出江西，建威將軍王戎出武昌，平南將軍胡奮出夏口，鎮南大將軍杜預出江陵，龍驤將軍王濬、廣武將軍唐彬率巴蜀之卒浮江而下，東西凡二十餘萬。
units.en: In the eleventh month: the conquest of Wu opened on every vector—Sima Zhou from Tu, Wang Hun from the north bank, Wang Rong, Hu Fen, Du Yu, and a river fleet under Wang Jun and Tang Bin—over two hundred thousand soldiers [24].
units.literal: In the eleventh month a great campaign was launched against Wu: Sima Zhou, general who guards the army and king of Langye, went out from Tu; Wang Hun, general who guards the east, from west of the river; Wang Rong, general who displays might, from Wuchang; Hu Fen, general who pacifies the south, from Xiakou; Du Yu, great general who guards the south, from Jiangling; Wang Jun, general who displays dragon prowess, and Tang Bin, general who displays martial breadth, led Ba–Shu troops down the Yangzi—more than two hundred thousand men on the eastern and western axes combined [24].

units.zh: 乙亥，以濬爲都督益、梁二州諸軍事，復下詔曰：「濬、彬東下，掃除巴丘，與胡奮、王戎共平夏口、武昌，順流長騖，直造秣陵，與奮、戎審量其宜。
units.en: On yihai, Wang Jun was made commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict was again issued, saying, "Jun and Bin shall go east, sweep away Baqiu, and together with Hu Fen and Wang Rong pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, drive swiftly down the current, and go straight to Moling; with Fen and Rong, carefully measure what is appropriate.
units.literal: On the day yihai Wang Jun was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict further said: “When Jun and Bin sail east, clear Baqiu, join Hu Fen and Wang Rong to pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, then drive straight down the stream to Moling with Fen and Rong coordinating as fits.

units.zh: 武昌既了，戎當以六千人增彬。
units.en: After Wuchang, Wang Rong was to reinforce Tang Bin with six thousand.
units.literal: Once Wuchang is settled, Rong should add six thousand men to Bin.

units.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。
units.en: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.
units.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.

units.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。
units.en: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.
units.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.

units.zh: 后遂荒淫放恣，與太醫令程據等亂彰內外。
units.en: She ran riot with physician Cheng Ju.
units.literal: Consort then wanton and dissolute—with Imperial Physician Cheng Ju and others licentious noise inner and outer.

units.zh: 故申生、衛伋、禦寇、楚建禀受形之氣，當嗣立之正，而猶如此。
units.en: Shensheng, Ji of Wei, Yu Kou, and Jian of Chu were lawful heirs—yet each met doom.
units.literal: Therefore Shensheng, Wei Ji, Yu Kou, and Chu Jian received their bodily qi with rightful claim to succession, yet still came to this.

units.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
units.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
units.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

units.zh: 西戎校尉司馬閻纘輿棺詣闕上書，以為：「漢戾太子稱兵拒命，言者猶曰罪當笞耳。
units.en: Yan Xun, Major under the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the palace gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, arguing: "When Emperor Wu's heir apparent Liu Ju took up arms in rebellion, critics still said his offense deserved only a beating.
units.literal: Yan Xun, Major of the Colonel of the Western Rong, came to the gate with his coffin on a cart and submitted a memorial, holding: "When the Han Heir Apparent Li raised troops and defied orders, those who spoke still said his crime merited only the bastinado.

units.zh: 纘，圃之孫也。
units.en: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.
units.literal: Xun was the grandson of Yan Pu.

units.zh: 孝惠皇帝上之下永康元年（
units.en: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Yongkang, year 1 (
units.literal: The lower portion of the first reign of Emperor Xiaohui, first year of Yongkang (

units.zh: 庚申，公元三零零年）
units.en: gengshen, CE 300)
units.literal: gengshen, common era year 300)

units.zh: 杜乂，字弘理，成恭皇后父，鎮南將軍預孫，尚書左丞錫之子也。
units.en: Du Yi, courtesy name Hongli, father of Empress Chenggong, was a grandson of Du Yu, South-Pacifying General, and son of Du Xi, Left Assistant Director in the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: Du Yi, styled Hongli, was the father of Empress Chenggong, grandson of South-Pacifying General Yu, and son of Left Assistant Director Xi.

units.zh: 或以潘岳《金穀詩序》方其文，羲之比于石崇，聞而甚喜。
units.en: Some likened his piece to Pan Yue's preface to the Golden Valley poems and compared Wang Xizhi himself to Shi Chong; he was delighted to hear it.
units.literal: Some with Pan Yue's "Jingu Poems Preface" compared his text; Xizhi compared to Shi Chong, hearing was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 恭王俊字道度，出嗣高密王略，官至散騎常侍。
units.en: Prince Gong Sima Jun, styled Daodu, continued Lue of Gaomi and rose to supernumerary cavalry attendant.
units.literal: Prince Gong Jun courtesy Daodu went out to succeed Prince of Gaomi Lue and reached irregular cavalry attendant.

units.zh: 泰四子：越、騰、略、模。
units.en: Four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.
units.literal: Tai had four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.

units.zh: 騰出後叔父，弟略立。
units.en: Teng was adopted out; Lue inherited.
units.literal: Teng went out to succeed uncle; younger brother Lue succeeded.

units.zh: 子孝王略
units.en: Prince Xiao Sima Lue.
units.literal: Son Prince Xiao Lue.

units.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
units.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
units.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
units.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
units.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

units.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
units.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
units.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

units.zh: 《晉起居注》裴頠議曰：「尊祖配天，其義明著，廟宇之制，理據未分。
units.en: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.
units.literal: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.

units.zh: 直可為一殿，以崇嚴祀，其餘雜碎，一皆除之。」
units.en: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."
units.literal: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."

units.zh: 元康初，湣懷太子在東宮，選大臣子弟有名稱者以為賓友，略與華恆等並侍左右。
units.en: Yuankang saw Lue among Minhuai's cultivated companions with Hua Heng.
units.literal: Early Yuankang Crown Prince Minhuai was in the eastern palace and chose sons of eminent ministers with reputation as guests and friends; Lue together with Hua Heng and others attended left and right.

units.zh: 若乃權君譎主，賢父慈親，猶有忠臣蹈功以罹禍，孝子抱仁以陷難，種、商、白起、孝己、伯奇，皆其類也。
units.en: Even under capricious fathers and sage parents, loyal servants still died for their deeds and filial sons for their love—Wen Zhong, Lord Shang, Bai Qi, Xiao Ji, and Boyi all belong to that tale.
units.literal: Yet twisted rulers and deceitful lords, worthy fathers and loving parents, still had loyal ministers who followed merit and met disaster, filial sons who embraced benevolence and fell into hardship—Wen Zhong, Bai Qi, filial Ji, Boyi—their kind.

units.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」
units.en: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."
units.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."

units.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿，遣東武公澹以千兵防衛太子，幽於許昌宮，令持書御史劉振持節守之，詔宮臣不得辭送。
units.en: An edict showed the confession to the ministers, sent Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, with a thousand troops to guard the heir apparent at Xuchang Palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, Attendant Secretary with credentials, to hold him under guard, forbidding palace officials to escort him on departure.
units.literal: An edict displayed the Yellow Gate confessor's testimony to the excellencies and ministers, dispatched the Duke of Dongwu Sima Dan with a thousand troops to guard the Heir Apparent, confined him at the Xuchang palace, ordered the Attendant Secretary with credentials Liu Zhen to hold him under guard, and decreed that palace officials might not take leave to escort him.

units.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子於小坊中，絕其食，宮人猶竊於牆上過食與之。
units.en: Lv told Liu Zhen, who moved him to a small compound and cut off food, though palace women still passed food over the wall.
units.literal: Lv reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen then moved the Heir Apparent to a small compound and cut off his food, yet palace women still secretly passed food over the wall.
